title: Button with Longest Push Time
statement:
A child presses buttons on a keyboard, and `events` records the presses in time order: `events[i] = [index_i, time_i]` means the button numbered `index_i` went down at moment `time_i`.

A press lasts from the moment of the press just before it until its own moment, so its duration is `time_i - time_(i-1)`. The first press is measured from moment `0`, so it lasts exactly `time_0`. Each press counts on its own; durations of the same button are never added together.

Return the button index of the press with the greatest duration. When several presses share that greatest duration, return the smallest button index among them.
notes:
## Intuition

A press's duration depends only on its own moment and the moment of the press right before it. So a single pass over `events` can work out each duration as it goes and remember the best press seen so far. A button pressed several times is judged press by press: its durations are compared one at a time, never summed.

## Approach

1. Start with the first press: `bestIndex` is its button and `longest` is its `time`, because it is measured from moment `0`.
2. For each later press `i`, read its `index` and `time`, and compute `duration = time - events[i - 1][1]`.
3. If `duration` beats `longest`, or equals it with an `index` smaller than `bestIndex`, make this press the best: update `longest` and `bestIndex`.
4. After the last press, return `bestIndex`.

## Example 1, step by step

`events = [[1,2],[2,5],[3,9],[1,15]]`. The first press gives `bestIndex = 1`, `longest = 2`.

- `i = 1`: button `2`, `duration = 5 - 2 = 3`, more than `2`, so `bestIndex = 2`, `longest = 3`.
- `i = 2`: button `3`, `duration = 9 - 5 = 4`, so `bestIndex = 3`, `longest = 4`.
- `i = 3`: button `1`, `duration = 15 - 9 = 6`, so `bestIndex = 1`, `longest = 6`.

The loop ends and the answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each press is looked at once.
- Space: O(1): only the best press so far is kept.

## Pitfalls

- The first press lasts `time_0`, not `0`. Skipping it misses Test 3, where the first press (10 units) is the longest.
- A tie goes to the smallest button index, not to the earliest press: `[[9,5],[3,10]]` (Test 5) answers `3`.
- Do not add up a button's presses. In Test 6 button `1` totals 7 units over three presses, but button `2`'s single 6-unit press is the longest.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bestIndex` | button of the longest press found so far |
| `longest` | duration of that press |
| `i` | position of the current press in `events` |
| `index`, `time` | button and moment of the current press |
| `duration` | how long the current press took |

narration.2: The first press is measured from moment 0, so its button starts as the answer...
narration.3: ...and its own time is the longest duration seen so far.
narration.4: Visit the remaining presses in time order.
narration.5: Read which button this press was and when it happened.
narration.6: This press lasted from the previous press's moment until its own.
narration.7: A strictly longer press wins; an equally long one wins only if its button index is smaller.
narration.12: Every press has been compared, so bestIndex is the button of the longest press.
